To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

28-Gb/ s transmission over 80 km uncompensated SMF and 400 km metro-ring networks can be enabled using inexpensive, 10-G Hz bandwidth, off-the-shelve optical components, IM/DD and a simplified MLSE-based receiver.
the proposed 28-Gb/ s IM/DD transmission system can be used in 100-G metro networks up to $400$ km, using a simplified MLSE receiver that is based on a reduced number of receiver states.

we have developed a cost-efficient 100-G metro-core and multispan metro ring network technology based on IM/DD and 10-GHz components that is capable of supporting up to 80-km point-to-point and up to 400-km multispan metro-ring links.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the generation, transmission, and detection of 28-Gbaud (28 Gb/s) intensity-modulated direct detection (IM/DD) signals over uncompensated links using off-the-shelf 10-GHz components and a digital signal-processing-based receiver.
the design of a 100 Gb Ethernet (GbE)-compliant, 4-lambda, 28-GbE/s, 100-GbE/s metro network employing the cost-efficient IM/DD technology.
the development of low-cost, high-performance 100-Gb/s transmission schemes for metro and access networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have demonstrated the generation and transmission, over uncompensated fibers, of 28-Gbps data using off-the-shelf 10-GHz bandwidth optical components, IM, DD, and a digital signal-processing receiver.
the proposed technology can be considered as the most promising candidate to enable the cost-efficient transition to next-generation, cost-efficient, high-capacity metro networks.
our proposed scheme is an enabler toward 100 Gb/ $s$ cost-efficient metro-core and metro-ring networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of the proposed transmitter, receiver, and signal processing techniques enables a cost-efficient 100-G metro network, which is an essential enabler for the transition to 100-G metro networks.
we are the first to demonstrate 100-G metro network transmission using IM/DD, 3-dB, and 10-GHz optical components.
we demonstrate that 100-G cost efficient metro networks are feasible with 28-Gb s data rate, IM/DD, 3 dB bandwidth limited components and a MLSE receiver.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by using a simple IM/DD scheme and low-cost components, we are able to achieve a 100-Gb/s data rate over metro distances, with performance close to what is achievable with coherent detection, and with an electronic dispersion compensation part that is significantly less complex than what is required for coherent detection.
the proposed solution enables a cost-efficient migration to 100 G in metro networks, which is of paramount importance for the industry.
the proposed technology can enable the transition to 100-G cost-effective metro networks without requiring expensive components or advanced optical modulation formats.
